evidence.label: Global Spherical Shells on Minimal Surfaces of Class VII

headline: Every minimal class VII surface with positive second Betti number contains a global spherical shell.
scope: Connected minimal compact complex surfaces with first Betti number one, Kodaira dimension minus infinity, and positive second Betti number.
plain: Class VII surfaces are compact complex surfaces that cannot carry a Kähler metric, and their classification has long been incomplete. A global spherical shell is a thin round piece of the punctured plane sitting inside such a surface. Nakamura’s program predicted that every minimal one with positive second Betti number contains such a shell. This paper claims to prove it. With Kato’s earlier work, that fixes these surfaces up to deformation.
doesNot: This does not treat the case of second Betti number zero, which was already classified, or non-minimal surfaces.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Ma. Kato, who introduced global spherical shells
scorecard.significanceWhy: If correct, it completes the classification of minimal class VII surfaces up to deformation.

explanation:
Take the complex plane of two variables with the origin removed. Shrink every point by half, z ↦ z/2, and treat a point and its half as the same point. What remains is a primary Hopf surface, a compact quotient of the punctured plane by a contraction[10]. One piece of it is the shell of points with size between 1/2 and 1. Gluing its inner sphere to its outer sphere gives the whole surface. As a smooth shape it is a circle times a three-sphere.

That surface has first Betti number 1: it has one independent loop that cannot shrink. Its second Betti number b₂ is 0. Now blow up points on it, replacing each point by a sphere of directions. Each blowup raises b₂ by one. After b blowups the Euler characteristic is b. A circle times a three-sphere has Euler characteristic 0, and each blowup adds 1.

Such surfaces belong to class VII. A compact complex surface is of class VII when it has first Betti number 1 and Kodaira dimension −∞[1]. These surfaces are never Kähler, so many standard tools do not apply. The case b₂ = 0 is classified: such minimal surfaces are Hopf or Inoue surfaces[2]. Minimal means there is no sphere of self-intersection −1 that could be blown down.

A global spherical shell is a copy of a thin neighbourhood of the unit three-sphere, sitting inside the surface. Its complement must be connected[14]. Kato introduced this structure in 1977[15]. In the Hopf example the round sphere of size 1 is such a shell. Nakamura’s classification program proposed that every minimal class VII surface with b₂ > 0 contains one[3].

This paper claims to prove that conjecture[4]. Every connected minimal class VII surface with positive second Betti number contains a global spherical shell[4]. By Kato’s earlier work, this fixes the shape of such a surface up to smooth deformation. The surface deforms to a primary Hopf surface blown up b₂ times, and its fundamental group is the whole numbers[5]. As a smooth shape it is a circle times a three-sphere, with b₂ reversed projective planes attached[5].

Earlier work reduced the conjecture to finding curves. Enoki’s theorem handles surfaces with a nonzero effective divisor of square zero[6]. Otherwise, Dloussky, Oeljeklaus and Toma showed that b₂ rational curves force a shell[7]. A rational curve is a curve whose smoothing is a sphere. So the task became producing enough rational curves[8]. Teleman proved the conjecture for b₂ = 1 using gauge theory[9]. He also found a cycle of curves when b₂ = 2[9].

The obstacle is that the surface may show no curves at first. The paper works on the infinite cyclic cover, which unrolls the one essential loop into an infinite chain of copies. There it builds holomorphic sections and takes their zero sets. The danger is that a zero set might have open, non-compact pieces that never close up[11]. The paper rules these out with estimates on long thin cylinders[12]. It then counts the resulting compact rational curves downstairs, and finds exactly b₂ of them[13]. The criterion of Dloussky, Oeljeklaus and Toma then gives the shell[13].

How sure is this? No Lean formalization is listed for this paper in the openai/math release. So no computer proof checker has checked it. No specialist review has been published.
hypeCheck: Major only if the proof holds. No Lean formalization is listed and no specialist review is published. The argument is long and analytic.

glossary.meaning: A compact complex surface with first Betti number one and Kodaira dimension minus infinity.
A count of independent holes of a given dimension in a shape.
A copy of a thin neighbourhood of the unit three-sphere, inside the surface, with connected complement.
A compact quotient of the punctured complex plane by repeated shrinking.
Having no sphere of self-intersection minus one that could be blown down.
A curve whose smoothing is a sphere.
Replacing a point by the sphere of all directions through it.
